article.title: The fate of pollen in two morphologically contrasting buzz-pollinated Solanum flowers
article.authors: Christian A. Vasquez-Castro; Elodie Morel; Bernardo Garcia-Simpson; Mario Vallejo-Marín

dataset.possible_blocker: Uncredentialed file access might be blocked; not evidence that source data do not exist

design.source_species_intervention: between species, not within-species architecture randomization
design.ground_recording_limit: Pollen lost to ground or air after leaving donor was not measured; only pollen collected under donor

source_definitions.C: anther grains remaining after single donor visit
source_definitions.D: pollen grains dislodged and recovered on ground under donor
source_definitions.F: pollen grains on bee corbiculae after trial
source_definitions.G: pollen grains remaining on bee body at end of trial
source_definitions.H: H1+H2+H3+H4 counted on four recipient stigmas
source_definitions.A: C+D+F+G+H (measured accounting reconstruction, not necessarily absolute biological production)
source_definitions.fractions: Pollen fate fractions D/B,F/B,G/B,H/B, all from the same one-donor one-bee trial
source_definitions.denominator_warning: Published species proportions are species means of trial-level ratios; never treat them as one shared measured joint draw

Solanum rostratum.architecture: heterantherous flower with a laterally displaced pollinating anther

Solanum dulcamara.architecture: monomorphic anthers fused into a cone

ground_dislodged_species_difference.interpretation: significant species contrast at original author reported test

basket_fraction_species_difference.interpretation: significant species contrast at original author reported test

release_visit_receipt_slope.warning: Original paper uses a negative binomial GLMM and four nested recipient flowers

species_recipient_order_interaction_comp.author_decision: additive preferred as more parsimonious; does not prove equal slopes

scientific_ceiling.same_species_as_earlier_BALANCE: S. rostratum appears in U3 and PR #276, and this programme shares Solanum context with PR #277 but is not a separate evolutionary transition
scientific_ceiling.different_bee_species_to_Wilkins_2022: Vasquez used B. terrestris; Wilkins used B. impatiens
